messages:
morgan: quick follow-up from the allocator-anchoring RFC — we need a concrete handshake for eviction/hand-off when operator wants to preempt a node. thoughts?

talia: yup, we saw churn last week when the operator force-evicted anchored slots. cache warming was lost and latency spiked :grimacing:

ryan: idea: introduce node-level anchors vs tenant anchors. node-anchor = runtime promise to keep a node 'warm' for Ns, tenant-anchor = logical mapping. operator can evict node-anchors only after a graceful handoff window.

anu: concern: long-lived tenant anchors can starve others. we should limit anchor credit (decay over time) and surface metrics.

jin: handshake sketch: allocator asks operator to 'reserve' target node with an idempotency token, operator returns lease token and estimated prewarm_ttl. if operator needs to evict, it uses lease token to request graceful drain from allocator. simple YAML for config:

```yaml
allocator_anchor:
  mode: soft  # soft vs hard
  ttl_sec: 45
  handoff_timeout_ms: 3000
  max_concurrent_handoffs: 5
```

morgan: sequence-of-events I had in mind:
1) allocator -> operator: /reserve-node {node_id, tenant, token}
2) operator ACKs with lease_token + prewarm_ttl
3) if operator needs capacity, operator -> allocator: /handoff {lease_token, reason}
4) allocator can try to move traffic / reassign within handoff_timeout, else operator evicts

dev-bot: metric update: anchor_reassign_rate jumped 3x during the last eviction wave — https://telemetry.example/anchors (automated)

talia: what are acceptance criteria? we should define SLO for successful handoff before eviction, and fallbacks if handoff fails.

ryan: acceptance ideas: >=95% handoffs complete within handoff_timeout in canary; anchor_reassign_rate decreases; no >1s P99 increase for affected tenants.

anu: fallback flow: if handoff fails, allocator can spawn a cold-prewarm request to burst-pool using tenant burst credits. billable but avoids SLA break. need to ensure we propagate backpressure signals so tenant isn't over-provisioning.

jin: implementation detail: lease_token must be opaque + single-use for operator->allocator handoff to avoid races. idempotency key on reserve request prevents dupes. one-liner: token = HMAC(allocator_id || node_id || nonce)

morgan: good call. also want to limit max_concurrent_handoffs per operator to avoid thundering. propose default max_concurrent_handoffs = 5 in config above.

talia: can we add metric anchor_handoff_latency and anchor_handoff_success? low-cardinality labels: tenant_tier, region.

ryan: agree. also expose anchor_credit_balance per tenant for fairness dashboards.

anu: ops question — what happens if operator crashes mid-handoff? operator should persist handoff state to k8s CRD and resume on restart, and allocator should time out after handoff_timeout + jitter.

jin: small proto for API endpoints:
POST /reserve-node -> {lease_token, prewarm_ttl}
POST /handoff -> {status: accepted|timeout|failed}
POST /cancel-reserve -> {status}

morgan: next steps: 1) prototype in a feature-flagged canary (single shard), 2) add metrics & alerts, 3) run chaos test: operator crash during handoff, 4) evaluate cost of fallback prewarm. can we sprint on this next week?

ryan: +1 from infra, I can pair on canary.

talia: i'll own metrics+dashboards.

anu: i'll write the fairness rules and credit decay algo.

jin: i'll sketch the minimal API server for operator.

morgan: amazing — I'll open a tracking RFC follow-up with the config defaults and acceptance criteria. thanks all :thumbsup:

talia: :heart:

dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary feature-flag 'allocator-anchor-handoff' enabled in cluster-canary-1
